content.comment_body: Hello, I’d like to know if it’s possible to connect a [company_name] [product_name] to a [company_name] [product_name] PLC or HMI using Profinet, so alarms from the PLC can be sent to the [company_name] [product_name], and then routed to an SMS alarm system. Could you provide an example of what the network setup might look like?
Could you please share the complete part number of the [product_name] module you’re using?
I haven’t started using it yet, but I’m considering whether it’s possible to connect [company_name] PLCs to a centralized SMS alarm system, exclusively using Profinet.

Hi. The current generation is [article_no], with a new version expected soon. [article_no] can join a Profinet network and exchange data. There are several ideas if you search—reviewing the system manual is quite useful. I'd encourage you to consider your options. The [version_no] can already perform this function with available modules, unless there’s a particular reason you prefer the [product_name] for this purpose. This is beyond my personal experience, but I’m sure others will be willing to help. If [version_no] meets your needs, do you still want to use [product_name]?

Thanks for your suggestions. Please check the drawing showing the current system in my brewery. It includes [company_name] [product_name] modules that collect alarms from the PLC and send them to an SMS alarm system. I’m considering a new SMS alarm setup that could help reduce the overall wiring.

Please try reattaching the drawing and remember to hit the "Upload Attachment" button after selecting your file. Sending texts via a mobile phone isn’t your only option—other wireless connections are available. There are even wireless repeaters capable of handling Profinet traffic. You might also find non-[company_name] products that support these features, depending on your location. I recommend starting a discussion in the Communication/Networks section, specifying your current hardware and asking for advice on going wireless. Personally, I’d still prefer a wired solution with a system-wide Ethernet line—wireless approaches may be costly and prone to interference from industrial equipment. I'm interested in seeing how your project develops. Feel free to update me with your progress. (Thanks) Best regards.

Hello, [product_name] doesn’t support Profinet. It uses S7-Com over TCP/IP, but both can operate within the same network. To solve this: 1. Review available examples on the [product_name] Internet page regarding [article_no]. You’ll find demonstrations for data exchange between [product_name] controllers. 2. In the PLC, select the required signals (diagnostic, etc.), then set a flag or marker that can be transferred to [product_name]. 3. For SMS notifications, you can use devices such as the INSYS IMO-1. The new [product_name] module can’t be used here, as it only supports GSM and GPRS. Please verify with your provider, especially in the US, if it’s still compatible. Hope this information is useful. [user_name]

Dear sir, Please take a look at the attached drawing. My goal is to collect alarms from all PLCs and transmit them to a centralized SMS alarm system for broadcasting to the engineering team at my brewery. The challenge is how to transfer alarms from the [company_name] PLCs to the [company_name] [product_name] using Profinet. [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are investigating how to connect [company_name] [product_name] modules with [company_name] PLCs via Profinet for a central SMS alarm system in a brewery. They encounter a major challenge: [product_name] does not support Profinet and instead operates using S7-Com over TCP/IP. This has caused confusion and a need for expert guidance about product compatibility, required protocols, and reducing wiring complexity in alarm workflows.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect effortless data exchange over Profinet between [company_name] [product_name] modules and [company_name] PLCs to manage alarms, aiming for straightforward integration with an SMS alarm broadcast system and minimal wiring.
